entity: HSBC UK Bank plc (the ring-fenced bank, consolidated) - the workbook perimeter
definition: RoTE is measured as reported profit attributable to the ordinary shareholders, excluding impairment of goodwill and other intangible assets for the period, divided by average reported equity adjusted for goodwill and intangibles. The adjustment to reported results and reported equity excludes amounts attributable to non-controlling interests. We provide RoTE in addition to RoE as a way of assessing our performance, which is closely aligned to our capital position. The measures are calculated in US dollars in line with the standard HSBC Group-wide calculation methodology.
source: HSBC UK Bank plc Annual Report and Accounts 2024, 'Reconciliation of alternative performance measures', section 'Return on equity and return on tangible equity', printed p.134 (PDF p.136), table 'Return on Equity and Return on Tangible Equity'
verification_note: Verified on a 300 dpi render 2026-10-10 of PDF p.136 (printed 134). The table's own build ($m): profit attributable to the ordinary shareholders of the parent company 4,989 (2023: 6,226); average shareholders' equity 33,100 (30,016); effect of average preference shares, AT1 and other equity instruments (2,808) ((2,726)); average ordinary shareholders' equity 30,292 (27,290); effect of goodwill and other intangibles net of deferred tax (5,549) ((5,342)); average tangible ordinary shareholders' equity 24,743 (21,948). The same two ratios also appear in the headline KPI table on PDF p.7, labelled 'Return on average ordinary shareholder's equity' and 'Return on average tangible equity'.
note: Struck in US DOLLARS, which the definition states outright, while the workbook reports in GBP - a ratio is unitless but the averaging is done on the USD series. The denominator is average ORDINARY shareholders' equity, i.e. total equity less preference shares, AT1 and other equity instruments, with the numerator correspondingly attributable to ordinary shareholders only, so it is not the computed ROE's total-equity base.
